analysis:
Docs-only PR. It documents a new `cluster_runtime` block (schema v2) in release registration and coordinator-side derivation of cluster approvals, grants and public parity qualifications.

Changed behavior described:
- provider-release.md head 651-792: facts are computed after notarization, with secrets stripped and the keychain removed. The app's CLI runs under `env -i`. The step fetches catalog/manifest/config from the lane's CDN/coordinator.
- A per-environment variable gates sending the block. Validation enforces the 128-byte ID bound and the 64 KiB body limit.
- Catalog capacity bounds: 64 approvals, 64 grants, 256 qualifications.
- configuration.md head 923-1008: v2 field table and public declaration. Qualifications promote to any Apple silicon pair. GLM schedule 2 is inert.
- configuration.md 1070-1076: the automatic approval source is noted.

The dev-branch lane (head 488-531, unenforced review on dev) is pre-existing, not changed here.

The coordinator handling cited by these docs (ParseReleaseClusterRuntime, NativeRuntimeCatalogWithReleases, parityQualification at platform df61dd6f) is outside the evidence. Strictness, catalog omission behavior and the any-pair promotion are unverified.

I reported one threat-model gap: release-key/CI authority over public cluster routing has no TB/T coverage. Cluster threats are absent from the canonical index.

No provider code was changed, so there is no direct regression to T-041, TB-011 or T-053.

Integration should check:
- whether the catalog/CDN fetch has integrity pins, since catalog `input_modalities` drive the vision/video envelope;
- whether head 867 ("highest active semver") conflicts with head 535-540 (non-SemVer ranking), which is a doc inconsistency affecting update discovery.

findings.detail:
Head lines 653-668 and 715-750 say a signed release's POST /v1/releases payload can carry `cluster_runtime`. A coordinator that accepts it derives build-pinned cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and promotable parity qualifications for public traffic. "No operator posts approvals, grants or public qualifications per build" (head 662). Before this change, a person copied these facts into the operator approval file.

The release key (A-005) and the CI pipeline now carry routing and public-traffic authority on top of binary/build identity (A-011, A-017). The payload content comes from the built app's own CLI (`env -i`, keychain removed first, head 675-684) and from fetched catalog/CDN `input_modalities`, which widen the media envelope (head 702-704).

Per head 663-666, a qualification applies to any Apple silicon pair regardless of numerics class. For GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B this rests on an owner decision, not on recorded parity. The dev lane (head 527-531) has no enforced review yet still registers with DEV_RELEASE_KEY. On DevNet, an unreviewed dev push with DEV_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED=true can therefore change public cluster routing.

TB-002, T-007, T-054 and A-018 do not describe cluster pairs, derived approvals or this authority path. Fix: add a cluster-runtime boundary or threat covering derivation from release payloads, catalog-sourced envelopes and the any-pair promotion policy. Require dev review before enabling the variable, and verify that the platform's strict parsing and catalog bounds back these docs.
findings.title: Release registration now authors cluster approvals and public-traffic qualifications; the threat model has no entry for this
